S = P ÷ 2

S = 40 ÷ 2

Q = P ÷ 4

Q = 40 ÷ 4

**Q = 10 kg**

R = 2 × Q

R = 2 × 10

**R = 20 kg**

Rod **"Q"** is the lightest among all.

questions.question: The mean of 11, 10, 12, 13, 15, x and 17, is 15. The value of x is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total observations (n) = 7 and Mean = 15.

Total Sum = Mean × n = 15 × 7 = 105.

Sum of known values = 11 + 10 + 12 + 13 + 15 + 17 = 78.

Value of x = Total Sum − Sum of known values = 105 − 78 = 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Observations are 11, 10, 12, 13, 15, x, 17. Mean = 15.

**Formula Used:** Mean = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

⇒ Number of observations (n) = 7

⇒ Sum = 78 + x

⇒ 15 = (78 + x) ÷ 7

⇒ 15 × 7 = 78 + x

⇒ 105 = 78 + x

⇒ x = 105 − 78

⇒ x = 27

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

Mean is the average calculated by summing all values and dividing by the count: Mean = (Σxᵢ) ÷ n.

Sum of Deviations

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero: Σ(xᵢ − Mean) = 0.

Weighted Mean

When values have different importance, the weighted mean is calculated as (Σwᵢxᵢ) ÷ Σwᵢ.</p

questions.question: What is the LCM of 0.126, 0.36 and 0.96?

Equalize the number of **decimal places**: 0.126, 0.360, and 0.960.

Remove decimals to get **integers**: 126, 360, and 960.

Find the **LCM** of these integers: LCM(126, 360, 960) = 20160.

Put the **decimal point** back after 3 places from the right.

Required LCM = 20.160 = 20.16.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.16.**

**Given:** Numbers are 0.126, 0.36, and 0.96.

**Formula Used:** **LCM of Decimals** = (LCM of integers with equal decimal places) ÷ 10ⁿ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b8244094ed3939b3c075dc6e6274a1d26cc8d337c6beff427e538f74eedc5b79.png] 

⇒ Convert given numbers to **like decimals** (3 decimal places): 0.126, 0.360, 0.960.

⇒ Identify the **integers** by removing the decimal: 126, 360, 960.

⇒ **Prime factorization** of 126 = 2¹ × 3² × 7¹.

⇒ **Prime factorization** of 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5¹.

⇒ **Prime factorization** of 960 = 2⁶ × 3¹ × 5¹.

⇒ **LCM** (126, 360, 960) = 2⁶ × 3² × 5¹ × 7¹.

⇒ **LCM** = 64 × 9 × 5 × 7 = 20160.

⇒ Put **decimal point** back after 3 places (since 0.126 has 3 places): 20160 ÷ 1000 = 20.16.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.16.**

• **Calcium sulphate** and its hydrates are inorganic compounds with the formula CaSO₄.

• Rani Rampal, the captain of the Indian women's hockey team, has been named **World Games Athlete of the Year 2019**, making her the first hockey player to win the prestigious award.
 
• The Indian government awarded her the **Padma Shri in 2020**.
 
• Rani won the Champion's Challenge Tournament in Kazan, Russia in June 2009, scoring four goals in the finals to lead India to victory.
 
• She was the youngest player in the national team that competed in the 2010 World Cup at the age of 15.

questions.question: In which year was the Jal Jeevan Mission launched in India? The mission aims at providing potable water through its scheme of functional household tap connections.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2019**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)** is the genesis of **the Rashtriya Jal Jeevan Kosh (RJJK)**, which is a flagship programme of the Government of India inaugurated by** the Hon'ble Prime Minister on August 15, 2019**.
 
• By 2024, it hopes to have 'Functional Household Tap Connections' (FHTC) installed in every rural household in the country.
 
• Approximately 19 crore rural households in the country will be provided with tap water as part of the effort.
 
• Since the commencement of the Jal Jeevan Mission, almost 5 crore rural families have been connected to running water (JJM).
 
• **The Rashtriya Jal Jeevan Kosh (RJJK) **is a registered public charitable trust established by the Ministry of Jal Shakti's Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation. 
 
• It was established to act as a collection point for philanthropic contributions and to enable such contributions for the establishment of safe drinking water supplies in villages.
 
• Tap water can also be provided at schools, anganwadi centres, tribal residential schools, health-and-wellness centres, and other locations.

questions.question: Rukmini Devi Arundale is a famous classical dancer of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale** was an Indian theosophist, **dancer and choreographer of Bharatanatyam, **an Indian classical dance form, and animal rights campaigner.
 
• She was the** first woman in Indian history to be elected to the Rajya Sabha**, the country's highest house of parliament.
 
• She was the most prominent revivalist of Bharatanatyam from** its original 'Sadhir' style, **which was popular among temple dancers, the Devadasis, and she also sought to restore old Indian arts and crafts.
 
• Rukmini Devi was named one of India Today's** "100 People Who Shaped India."**
 
• In 1956, she received the Padma Bhushan, and in 1967, she received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a significant Hindu form of Indian classical dance.
 
• **The initial sources of Bharatanatyam **are regarded to be Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra and Nandikeshvara's Abhinaya Darpana (Mirror of Gesture) (an Indian classical dance form).
 
• The dance form is also briefly addressed in Someshwara III's Kannada work Manasollasa.
 
• Since ancient times, it has thrived in the temples and courts of southern India.
 
• It is one of eight well-known Indian classical dance genres that reflects South Indian religious themes and spiritual ideals, particularly those of Shaivism, Vaishnavism, and Shaktism, collectively known as Hinduism.

questions.question: An official enumeration of population done periodically is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**census**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A census** is a periodic** official enumeration of the population**.
 
• **The first census in India** was conducted in 1872. However, the first complete census was done in 1881.
 
• Since then, every ten years, censuses have been held. The most thorough source of demographic, social, and economic statistics is the Indian Census.
 
• The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, conducts a census every ten years.
 
• In 2021, India will conduct its 16th census.
 
• **Union Home Minister Amit Shah **announced in September 2019 that the 2021 national census would be conducted entirely digitally via a mobile phone application. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Any statistical component that influences population growth or decline can be included in** demographics**, although six characteristics are particularly important: **population size, density, age structure, fecundity (birth rates), mortality (death rates), and sex ratio (Dodge 2006). **
 
• **The Citizenship Act of 1955 **was amended in 2003, requiring the development of the **National Register of Citizens (NRC)**. Its goal is to identify and expel illegal immigrants by documenting all legal citizens of India.
 
• **The National Population Register (NPR)** is a database of people who live in a hamlet, rural region, town, ward, or delimited area within a ward in a city or town.

questions.question: Who is the chairperson of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Vice-President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Vice-President of India** is the **chairperson of the Rajya Sabha**.
 
• **Muppavarapu Venkaiah Naidu **is an Indian politician who has been serving as India's vice president since 2017.
 
• He formerly served in the Modi Cabinet as the minister of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation, Urban Development, and Information and Broadcasting.
 
• He was a senior member of the Bharatiya Janata Party and the party's national president from 2002 to 2004.
 
• He formerly served in the Atal Bihari Vajpayee cabinet as the Union Cabinet Minister for Rural Development.
 
• On August 11, 2017, he was sworn in as** the Vice President of India and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.**
 
• He earned 516 votes, compared to 244 for UPA candidate **Gopalkrishna Gandhi.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The vice president of India** is the** deputy to the president of India**, who is the head of state of the Republic of India.
 
• After the president, the vice president is the second-highest constitutional office, ranking second in order of precedence and first in line of succession to the presidency.
 
• The vice president determines whether a bill is a money bill or not when it is introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• He will send a measure filed in the Rajya Sabha to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha if he believes it is a money bill.

questions.question: Which state among the following is the largest producer of coffee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karnataka** is the **largest producer of coffee**.
 
• With **203,445 MT** of coffee output in 2019-20, the state produced over** 70% of India's total coffee production**.
 
• Karnataka's major coffee variety is Robusta, however, the state also produces a limited amount of Arabica.
 
• The state has ideal climatic conditions for coffee plantations, including high altitude, sloppy mountains, and adequate rainfall.
 
• The coffee plantation is located in the Karnataka districts of Chikkamagaluru, Hassan, and Kodagu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Coffee cultivation** in India dates back to the 16th-century Sufi mystic Baba Budan, who returned from Yemen with "seven seeds" of "Mocha" coffee beans and planted them on "Baba Budan Giris" in Karnataka.
 
• Coffee plantations gradually spread over south India, and commercial coffee plantations began in the 18th century.
 
• Coffee is grown mostly in the southern Indian states of **Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is also grown in India's northeastern states.
